title: Drift Fracture
statementMarkdown:
A legacy stabilizer claims the reading $f(n) = n^2 + n + 41$ stays indivisible for every cycle $n$.

The claim is a lie. **Find the first cycle $n$ where $f(n)$ splits into a product of two smaller positive integers.**
hints: Test small cycles — the stabilizer holds up longer than you would expect.
At the fracture point, the value is a perfect square: $41 \times 41$.
